task_instance: Given a small TypeScript module (orderSummary.ts) with the kinds of issues the skill targets (nested ternary for status precedence, a redundant isNotEmpty(arr) wrapper around arr.length > 0, a dense filter/map/reduce one-liner, arrow functions instead of function declarations, missing explicit return types) and a CLAUDE.md defining project standards, apply the code-simplifier skill's refinement principles to rewrite the module for clarity while preserving exact behavior, then verify functional equivalence with a test harness run against both versions.
evidence: Created work/CLAUDE.md (project standards), work/orderSummary.before.ts (messy version) and work/test.ts (behavioral test covering status precedence, positive-amount summing, and empty-orders edge case). Compiled and ran the before version with `npx tsc --target es2019 --module commonjs --outDir dist_before orderSummary.ts test.ts && node dist_before/test.js` -> all 4 assertions PASS. Rewrote work/orderSummary.ts applying the skill's principles: replaced the nested ternary (isCancelled ? ... : isRefunded ? ... : isPaid ? ... : 'pending') with an if/else chain in a named function with an explicit OrderStatus return type; removed the redundant isNotEmpty(arr) abstraction in favor of a direct orders.length === 0 check; split the compact `.filter().map().reduce()` one-liner into named intermediate steps; converted arrow functions to `function` declarations with explicit return type annotations, matching CLAUDE.md's stated standards. Compiled and ran the after version the same way (dist_after/test.js) -> all 4 assertions PASS, and `diff <(node dist_before/test.js) <(node dist_after/test.js)` reported IDENTICAL OUTPUT, confirming behavior-preserving simplification. Files: work/CLAUDE.md, work/orderSummary.before.ts, work/orderSummary.ts, work/test.ts.
